pl-l4d15c6-d1e112.summary: Draws out that those remaining in mortal sin, though they give large alms, do not satisfy through them, acting out of order by not beginning with themselves; nor is such work properly alms, since they are cruel to themselves and do not please God. So satisfaction done for one sin while persisting in another is not satisfaction, since fasting, prayer, and good works profit nothing unless the mind turns from sin; and if, converted, he confesses the hidden sin, satisfaction must be imposed for both, since he did not worthily satisfy for the first.
claims: Alms while persisting in mortal sin are not satisfaction.
Satisfaction must be imposed for both sins.

pl-l4d15c6-d1e118.summary: Reports some who think it was satisfaction, but fruitless while he persists in the other sin; its fruit is received when he repents of the other sin, when both are forgiven and the preceding dead satisfaction is revived, as baptism begins to profit one who approached insincerely when insincerity departs.
claims: Some hold the earlier satisfaction revives with later penance.

pl-l4d15c6-d1e121.summary: Notes that they support this opinion with authorities.

pl-l4d15c6-d1e124.summary: Quotes Augustine: it is pious to believe, and our faith requires, that when Christ's grace destroys earlier evils in a man, it also rewards goods; destroying what it did not find its own, it loves the good it planted in the sinner.
claims: Grace rewards the good it planted in the sinner.

pl-l4d15c6-d1e134.summary: Quotes Jerome: if you see someone among many sins doing some just works, God is not so unjust as to forget the few goods for the many evils; he will make him reap what he sowed in good ground.
claims: God does not forget good works amid sins.

pl-l4d15c6-d1e143.summary: Interprets these as concerning one who at one time does good in charity and is good, and at another time is bad and sins much: not doing just works amid sins at the same time, but both at different times, since unless he were good when doing good, he would not be said to sow in good ground. When the later evils are destroyed by penance, the earlier goods done in charity, killed by those evils, are revived and rewarded.
claims: The authorities concern good done in charity at an earlier time.
Earlier good works revive through penance.

pl-l4d15c6-d1e146.summary: Cites Hebrews: 'laying the foundation of penance from dead works', calling 'dead works' earlier good works killed by later sin; as sinning makes them void, penance revives them and they begin to profit for eternal merit. Likewise God loves the good he planted in the sinner, one who sinned after that good, not one sinning and doing good at once, whose work God would not love for reward.
claims: 'Dead works' are earlier goods killed by sin, revived by penance.

pl-l4d15c6.summary: Concludes that those remaining in mortal sin, though they give generous alms, do not thereby make satisfaction, since they act out of order, not beginning with themselves; such works are not properly alms. So satisfaction for one sin while persisting in another is not satisfaction, and when the hidden sin is later confessed, satisfaction must be imposed for both. Some think the earlier satisfaction was real but fruitless, reviving when the other sin is repented, like baptism received insincerely, citing Augustine and Jerome on God rewarding good done amid sins. Lombard reads those authorities as concerning good done in charity at one time and later killed by sin, which revives through penance; Hebrews' 'dead works' are earlier good works killed by later sin.
claims: Alms while persisting in mortal sin are not satisfaction.
Satisfaction for one sin while retaining another must be repeated for both.
Some hold the earlier satisfaction revives when the other sin is repented.
Good works done in charity and later killed by sin revive through penance.
